title: Split `Lint & Repo Gates` into parallel lanes behind an aggregator, the way `TypeScript Type Check` already is: 193 serial steps are 28 minutes of every PR's critical path and one step is 41% of them
body:
## The measurement

`Lint & Repo Gates` is the longest job in this repository's CI and it is the critical path: every other job finishes in 12 minutes or less and they all run in parallel with it.

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `Lint & Repo Gates` duration | 28 minutes |
| steps in it | 193, all sequential |
| longest single step, `PM dispatch-gates self-test` | 692 s, **41%** of the job |
| next four steps | 116 s, 100 s, 72 s, 61 s |
| PRs merged in the trailing 7 days | 633 (about 90 a day) |
| cost of the PR leg alone | about 295 compute-hours a week |

Taken at head `dc82eaf` of objectstack-ai/objectstack#19642, run of 2026-09-22T05:47Z.

⛔ This card does not propose removing, weakening or skipping a single check. Measured on the same window, the PR leg of this workflow fails on **12 of 100 runs** across 8 distinct branches, so it is catching real defects at a rate of roughly eleven a day. The job's CONTENT earns its place. Its SHAPE does not: 193 steps run one after another when almost none of them depend on the one before.

## Why this is the cheap change

Three of the four other heavy jobs in this repository are already split, and one of them carries the exact pattern this card asks for. `Type Check` is four separate jobs — `typecheck-source-gates`, `typecheck-workspace`, `typecheck-debt`, `typecheck-consumers` — plus a fifth job named `TypeScript Type Check` whose whole body is `needs:` on the other four. That fifth job is the one the branch protection requires; it takes zero minutes and stands in for the lanes behind it.

That solves the hazard this card would otherwise carry. `Lint & Repo Gates` is one of the seven required contexts, and AGENTS.md is explicit that a required context is matched by check-run NAME, so a rename detaches its gate silently. The aggregator pattern keeps the name: the lanes get new names, and a job still called `Lint & Repo Gates` waits on them. **No branch-protection setting changes, and nothing can ride through green as an advisory check-run.**

The pattern also ships its own anti-drift control, which this card must adopt rather than reinvent: the aggregator declares a ROSTER in real YAML, `scripts/check-aggregator-roster.mjs` asserts statically that the roster equals the job's `needs:` in both directions, and the aggregate re-checks the same equality at run time against `toJSON(needs)`. Without it, a lane added and forgotten rides green behind a context that appears required and blocks nothing.

## What to do

1. Group the 193 steps into lanes by what they read, not by duration. `PM dispatch-gates self-test` (692 s) belongs alone or with the other PM-tooling self-tests: it re-spawns its own CLI as a child process many times against the real checkout and builds temporary git repositories, so it shares almost nothing with the source-scanning gates.
2. Give each lane its own job and its own `needs:`-free setup, exactly as the `typecheck-*` lanes do.
3. Keep a job named **exactly** `Lint & Repo Gates` whose body is the roster declaration plus the verdict step.
4. Wire the roster into `scripts/check-aggregator-roster.mjs` so the new aggregate is held to the same equality as the existing one.

## Acceptance

- The seven required contexts are unchanged by name; branch protection is not edited.
- Every step that runs today still runs, on the same triggers. ⛔ Nothing is dropped, skipped or moved behind a paths filter as part of this card.
- `check-aggregator-roster.mjs` covers the new aggregate, and a lane added without a roster entry is red.
- Wall-clock for the aggregate measured on a real PR is reported in the PR body against the 28-minute reading above. The expected landing zone is the longest single lane, which is bounded below by the 692 s step until that step is separately optimised.
- ⛔ Out of scope: making `dispatch-gates.mjs`'s self-test faster. Its cost is real and has a documented reason (its companion gate's header explains why a fixture cannot prove the point); this card only stops it from holding 192 other steps behind it.
